title: XRR fitting preset
description: Laboratory-, instrument- and material-specific constants for the XRR fitting procedure. The procedure text carries only general rules and refers to the keys defined here. One preset describes one instrument at one laboratory.

preset_id.description: Stable identifier. Reported in slot 1 with the SHA-256 of this file's raw bytes.

provenance.description: Where these constants come from. A value with no measured source must say so here.

lambda_A.description: The wavelength the fit uses. With an unresolved K-alpha doublet (no crystal monochromator) this is the intensity-weighted mean of K-alpha1 and K-alpha2, because an unresolved doublet peaks at its centroid.

resolution_deg.description: Delta-theta FWHM in degrees theta. NOT fittable: the engine refuses it. Chosen by a chi-squared re-fit scan (scan_step) and never inherited from another operator's project file. The scanned value conditions the calculated curve to this measurement (it also absorbs the smoothing pass); it is not a measured beam divergence.

scan_step.description: Step of the resolution scan. After a fit converges it is re-fitted at each value from min to max in this step and the lowest chi-squared is kept, because the fringe contrast is one feature of the curve while the chi-squared is over the whole fitting range.

auto_theta_max_deg.description: Angle below which the automatic scale looks for the measured maximum: the end of the total-reflection plateau.

substrate.description: Substrates live in a separate library so several can be in use at once; a job names one by id. Held fixed either way: the engine does not fit the substrate.

materials.description: Density and roughness bounds and start values for layers of the design. Any material not listed in named takes default_rule, so a new material system needs no new text. The light and heavy materials of a period are properties of the job's design, not of this preset.

sigma_A.description: Roughness (sigma, in A) bounds and start range for every layer of a stack, whatever its material. The single-film exception is single_film.sigma_bounds_A; the substrate and the surface layer carry their own. A laboratory value, not a physical constant: say in reason where it comes from.

start.description: Range the start value is drawn from, inside bounds.

surface.description: The light surface overlayer the procedure adds. Distinct from a cap belonging to the design, which is taken from the design.

contamination_layer.description: Carries its own bounds, which are NOT the material bounds of `materials`: a hydrocarbon overlayer is lighter than the sputtered form of the same element.

sensitivity_variant.description: The deliberately thicker, denser overlayer used as a sensitivity variant in section 3. It must differ from the starting layer or the variant probes nothing.

chi2.description: Weighting of the engine's chi-squared, per stack type: a single film and a multilayer are not weighted alike. Changing any of these changes what a chi-squared threshold means.

paired.description: Parameters that keep one value over all periods in a profile fit, for every layer.

seeds.description: Every fit is run from several optimizer seeds. The spread of a parameter across the seeds is what the curve leaves undetermined, so it is measured rather than assumed.

list.description: Explicit seeds, so a run is reproducible to the last digit. Length must equal count.

lock_interlayer_thickness.description: Profile fits: when true, the thickness of every layer the design marks as an interlayer keeps one value over all periods, like the parameters in paired; only the main layers' thicknesses carry a depth profile. Interdiffusion does not drift through the stack when the growth temperature is constant, while deposition rates do.

reporting.description: How a fit is turned into a reported result: what counts as determined, and when a richer model is preferred to a simpler one.

sum_not_split.description: When true, adjacent layers whose thicknesses trade against one another across seeds are reported as their sum, with the split declared undetermined.

undetermined_precision.description: A parameter whose spread across seeds exceeds the value here is reported as undetermined rather than as a number.

model_selection.description: A richer model (profile over periodic, a higher polynomial order) is preferred only when it beats the simpler model's chi-squared by this many times the simpler model's own seed-to-seed chi-squared spread. Below that the difference is not distinguishable from the optimizer's own scatter.

single_film.description: Exceptions that apply when the specimen is one film rather than a stack.

theta_min_deg.description: Lower end of the fitting range for a single film of the light material, where the simulated edge shows a shoulder the measurement does not have.

acceptance.description: Thresholds the FITTER applies to its own fit in section 10. A threshold carries no further than the conditioning it was fixed under, which calibrated_under records. Agreement tolerances against a withheld reference fit are a different thing and do not belong here: they are the experimenter's, not the fitter's.

scale_solve.description: Whether chi2_max was fixed with the scale solved (true) or anchored (false). A solved chi-squared is never higher than the anchored one for the same structure, so a threshold fixed under one does not carry to the other.

scale_solve_window.description: The solve window chi2_max was fixed under when scale_solve is true (fit_xrr scale_solve_window); part of the conditioning, because a narrower window can clamp the solve and raise the chi-squared.

order_visible_factor.description: A Bragg order counts as visible when its measured maximum stands this many times above the background.

chi2_conditioning_alarm.description: Above this, the conditioning is wrong rather than the model.

interfaces.description: How the two interfaces of a period are treated. One specular curve cannot divide an interlayer between them. Growth is often asymmetric, but not always and not unconditionally: an asymmetry that holds while the heavy layer grows crystalline can vanish once that layer is thin enough to stay amorphous, so a declaration carries the condition under which it holds. A constraint may also come from a method other than reflectivity, such as TEM or XPS, which is recorded as its evidence.

mode.description: explore: no assignment is assumed; the fit is run under each admissible assignment and all are reported with their chi-squared, the split staying undetermined unless a criterion excludes one. constrained: declarations in pairs are applied where their condition holds, and the split is reported as constrained by the declaration.

pairs.description: Keyed by material pair, e.g. "W/B4C". A pair absent here is treated as explore whatever the mode.

constraint.description: wider_on: one interface carries the wider interlayer, named in wider_interface. symmetric: the two interlayers are equal, which is the case when neither layer orders. undetermined: explicitly no constraint, recorded so that silence is distinguishable from a considered decision.

wider_interface.description: Required when constraint is wider_on. Written "<deposited> on <grown upon>", e.g. "W on B4C".

ratio_min.description: Optional least ratio of wider to narrower, applied as a bound. Omit when only the ordering is known.

applies_when.description: Condition under which the declaration holds, tested against the fitted structure after the fit. When it fails, the declaration does not apply and the pair falls back to explore.

heavy_thickness_A_min.description: The declaration holds only while the heavy layer is at least this thick, i.e. thick enough to order rather than remain amorphous.

evidence.description: What produced the constraint. A constraint with no method is a prior smuggled in as a result.

smoothing.description: Smoothing of the MEASURED curve before the residual is formed (the engine's smooth {"passes": n}). It is not a chi-squared weighting and not a property of the model; it changes the data the fit sees.

passes.description: Number of moving-average passes over the measured curve. 0 = off. No count threshold is offered: the benchmark found no brightness at which a pass earns its place, so there is nothing to switch on.

fitting_range.description: Where the fitting range ends (section 6 rule 4). The range covers at least this many Bragg orders as PREDICTED by the refined period, visible or not, and never runs past the measured end; with that many or more visible it ends half a spacing past the last visible order, as procedure v5 always did.

min_predicted_orders.description: Count of predicted orders the range must cover. 7 for this laboratory: the count its bright curves show, and the endpoint at which the benchmark gain has its minimum (FINDINGS R10).

scale.description: The scale of the measured curve (section 4). The anchor is set by normalization at the plateau maximum; with solve true the engine then scores every candidate structure at the multiplier of that anchor which minimises its chi-squared, found in closed form and held within a factor of (1 + solve_window) of the anchor either way (fit_xrr scale_solve and scale_solve_window).

solve.description: Sent as fit_xrr scale_solve. True: the scale is profiled out within the window. False: the anchored scale is used as it stands, which reproduces numbers from before the option existed.

solve_window.description: Sent as fit_xrr scale_solve_window: |log10(solved / anchored)| <= log10(1 + solve_window). 0 pins the scale to the anchor. A fit whose scale ends on the bound reports scale_clamped true.
